newsitem.title: USA: Judge says Marvel holders can vote for directors.
newsitem.headline: Judge says Marvel holders can vote for directors.

text.p: A federal judge in Delaware ruled Wednesday that bondholders of Ronald Perelman's Marvel Holdings Inc are entitled to vote their 80 percent stake in Marvel Entertainment Group Inc to elect directors.

The decision by Judge Roderick McKelvie of the U.S. District Court in Delaware reverses a bankruptcy judge's restraining order barring creditors from voting as shareholders to decide the fate of a debtor's assets.

McKelvie delayed the effective date of his ruling by 10 days to give Marvel and Chase Manhattan Bank, the lead bank for most senior secured lenders in the Marvel bankruptcy filings, a chance to seek "relief" from his ruling.
At issue in the bondholder vote is which of two competing reorganization plans will prevail as Marvel tries to emerge from chapter 11 protection for which it filed in December.

Under a plan favored by the banks, Marvel would merge with Toy Biz Inc, giving the banks and other secured lenders the proceeds from a $250 million loan plus a $170 million note and all the stock of Marvel units Fleer, Skybox and Panini.

The plan of lead bondholder Carl Icahn calls for an infusion of $365 million, with $100 million of that going to the banks and the rest used to pay unsecured creditors and operate the reorganized business.

"The real question is when does Icahn sit down with the banks?" a source close to the case told Reuters "How much of any new money will be used to pay down the banks and how much will be used to operate the new company?"

The source said the next step is for Marvel and the banks to convince Judge Balick of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware by arguing this time that, unless the vote is enjoined, Marvel assets will be harmed. Failing that, the banks can try to appeal McKelvie's decision.

In his decision, McKelvie addressed the issue of harm by saying that, even if shareholders' action is "motivated by a desire to arrogate more bargaining power in the negotiation of a reorganization plan...does not constitute clear abuse."

A Marvel spokesman said: "We have not seen the ruling so we don't know the basis for the judge's decision. The fact that he has given us 10 days provides opportunity for Marvel to seek available remedies to prevent the bondholders from seizing control of the company."
